personality_one_liner: A tactical, high-performance command center for on-the-go coding.

spacing.rule: Dense and structural. Keep generous margins for touch targets, but use tight sm/md spacing between code lines, file items, and console outputs to maximize visible information.

dont's: No blur or glassmorphism. This is a dense data/utility screen. Clarity and performance beat aesthetics. Use solid surfaceSecondary for elevation.

screens.name: Code Editor (Main)
screens.purpose: The core coding workspace where users write, edit, and run code.

states.loading: Centered brandPrimary spinner against surface background.
states.empty: No file open. Show the 'floating cubes' illustration in the center, with 'Open a file from the explorer' in onSurfaceSecondary, and a primary CTA 'Toggle Explorer'.
states.error: File unreadable error overlay with a 'Retry' action.

screens.layout: Use a Stack navigator wrapped inside a Drawer navigator. The Drawer holds the File Explorer. The main screen contains the Editor. The Header holds a hamburger menu (left), current filename in JetBrains Mono (center), and a 'Play/Run' brandPrimary icon button (right). Below the header, split the view horizontally: left gutter (surfaceSecondary) for line numbers, right area (surface) for code input. At the bottom of the screen, pinned above the keyboard, place a horizontally scrollable quick-action bar for coding symbols ({, }, (), ;, ").

screens.name: File Explorer (Drawer)
screens.purpose: Navigate directories, create files, and toggle local/cloud sync.

states.loading: Skeleton text lines matching the file tree structure.
states.empty: 'No files in project' text with an 'Add File' ghost button.

screens.layout: Occupies the left drawer. Header displays the workspace name. Below it, a list of files/folders. Active file uses a brandTertiary tinted background with a 2px brandPrimary left border. At the absolute bottom of the drawer, pin a settings row containing the 'Local/Cloud Sync' toggle switch.

screens.name: Code Runner Console (Bottom Sheet)
screens.purpose: Displays stdout and stderr when a file is executed.

states.error: N/A - Errors are printed directly as stderr text.

screens.layout: Triggered by the Run button. Uses @gorhom/bottom-sheet popping over the editor. The sheet background is surfaceSecondary. Header has 'Console' and a 'Clear' icon. Content area is a scrollable text view. Standard output uses onSurface; error output uses the error color. Font is exclusively JetBrains Mono.

screens.name: AI Assistant (Chat)
screens.purpose: Multi-turn Gemini 3 Pro chat to explain, ask, or generate code.

states.empty: Center the glowing cubes illustration with a prompt 'How can Gemini assist your code today?'
states.error: Message failed to send indicator next to the failed bubble.

screens.layout: Can be accessed via a FAB or a header action in the editor. Classic chat layout. User bubbles are surfaceTertiary; AI bubbles are surfaceSecondary with a subtle brandPrimary top-border. Bottom input area contains a TextInput and a Send button. When the AI generates code, it must be presented in a syntax-highlighted block (surface) with a 'Copy' and 'Insert at Cursor' button.

ai_empty_state.alt: Floating glowing geometric cubes in the dark

instructions_to_main_agent: Strictly follow the Dark-First Utility guidelines. No blur, no glassmorphism, no rounded playful UI. The app should feel like a tactical terminal.
Do not use any shade of blue, purple, or indigo anywhere in the app. Stick to the provided warm Amber (brandPrimary) and deep Obsidian grays.
Implement the File Explorer inside a Drawer Navigator. The active file should have a brandTertiary background with a hard left border.
The Code Runner Console MUST be a bottom sheet (`@gorhom/bottom-sheet`) that overlays the editor when 'Run' is tapped. It should not be a separate screen.
Include a horizontal scrollable tool strip anchored to the top of the keyboard (or bottom of the editor) for quick insertion of common coding symbols like brackets and semicolons.
For the code editor and console outputs, strictly use the JetBrains Mono font to ensure code is properly monospaced. Use IBM Plex Sans for general UI text.
The AI Assistant must have an 'Insert at Cursor' action for code blocks to seamlessly inject Gemini's response directly into the active editor file.
